requirement: Regulations in this subpart apply to activities associated with the Ocean Wind 1 project.
scope: Ocean Wind 1 project offshore of New Jersey

requirement: Impact pile driving of wind turbine generator (WTGs) and offshore substation (OSSs) foundations; vibratory pile driving (install and subsequently remove) of cofferdams and goal posts; high-resolution geophysical (HRG) site characterization surveys; unexploded ordnances or munitions and explosives of concern (UXOs/MECs) detonation.
scope: Construction phase, wind turbine foundations and offshore substations
related_domains: marine mammal protection; construction activities; environmental impact assessment

requirement: The incidental take of marine mammals by the activities listed in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section is limited to the following species.
scope: BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0498, export cable routes, and sea-to-shore transition points in New Jersey.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; environmental impact assessment

requirement: Take by mortality or serious injury of any marine mammal species is not authorized.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; environmental impact assessment

requirement: By Level B harassment associated with the acoustic disturbance of marine mammals by impact pile driving (WTG and OSS foundation installation), vibratory pile driving (cofferdam and goal post installation and removal), UXO/MEC detonations, and HRG site characterization surveys.
scope: Construction activities related to wind turbine generators and offshore substation foundations.

requirement: By Level A harassment associated with the acoustic disturbance of marine mammals by impact pile driving of WTG and OSS foundations and UXO/MEC detonations.
scope: Construction activities related to wind turbine generators and offshore substation foundations.

requirement: LOA Holder must implement the mitigation measures contained in this section and any LOA issued under §§ 217.266 and 217.267.
scope: Activities identified in § 217.260(c) within the area described in § 217.260(b)
related_domains: marine mammal protection; environmental impact assessment

requirement: A copy of any issued LOA must be in the possession of LOA Holder and its designees, all vessel operators, visual protected species observers (PSOs), passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) operators, pile driver operators, and any other relevant designees operating under the authority of the issued LOA.
LOA Holder must conduct training for construction, survey, and vessel personnel and the marine.
A description of the training program must be provided to NMFS at least 60 days prior to the initial training before in-water activities begin.

Prior to and when conducting any in-water activities and vessel operations, LOA Holder personnel and contractors must use available sources of information on North Atlantic right whale presence in or near the Project Area.
The marine mammal monitoring team must monitor these systems no less than every 4 hours.
related_domains: marine mammal monitoring; environmental impact assessment

requirement: For any UXO/MEC detonation, these systems must be monitored for 24 hours and immediately prior to blasting.
For North Atlantic right whales, any visual or acoustic detection must trigger a delay to the commencement of pile driving, UXO/MEC detonation, and HRG surveys.

If a large whale is sighted or acoustically detected that cannot be confirmed as a non North Atlantic right whale, it must be treated as if it were a North Atlantic right whale for purposes of mitigation.
If a delay to commencing an activity is called for by the Lead PSO or PAM operator, LOA Holder must take the required mitigative action.

If a shutdown of an activity is called for by the Lead PSO or PAM operator, LOA Holder must take the required mitigative action unless shutdown would result in imminent risk of injury or loss of life to an individual, pile refusal, or pile instability.

The activity must not commence or resume until the animal(s) has been confirmed to have left and is on a path away from the Level B harassment zone or after 15 minutes for small odontocetes and pinnipeds, and 30 minutes for all other species with no further sightings;
scope: Construction phase, Level B harassment zone

requirement: If a marine mammal is on a path towards or comes within 10 meters (m) (32.8 feet) of equipment, LOA Holder must cease operations until the marine mammal has moved more than 10 m on a path away from the activity to avoid direct interaction with equipment;

All vessels must be equipped with a properly installed, operational Automatic Identification System (AIS) device and LOA Holder must report all Maritime Mobile Service Identify (MMSI) numbers to NMFS Office of Protected Resources;

By accepting the issued LOA, LOA Holder consents to on-site observation and inspections by Federal agency personnel (including NOAA personnel) during activities described in this subpart, for the purposes of evaluating the implementation and effectiveness of measures contained within the LOA and this subpart;
LOA Holder must comply with the following vessel strike avoidance measures, unless an emergency situation presents a threat to the health, safety, or life of a person.
scope: Specified geographical region during project activities involving vessels.

requirement: Prior to the start of the Project's activities involving vessels, LOA Holder must receive a protected species training that covers, at a minimum, identification of marine mammals that have the potential to occur where vessels would be operating.
scope: Training requirement for personnel involved in project activities.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection

requirement: LOA Holder's vessels, regardless of their vessel's size, must maintain a vigilant watch for all marine mammals.
scope: Operational phase of the project involving vessels.

requirement: All LOA Holder's vessels must transit at 10 kn or less within any active North Atlantic right whale.
scope: Active North Atlantic right whale areas during vessel transit.

requirement: All LOA Holder's vessels, regardless of size, must immediately reduce speed to 10 kn or less for at least 24 hours when a North Atlantic right whale is sighted at any distance by any project-related personnel or acoustically detected by any project-related PAM system.

If a North Atlantic right whale is reported via any of the monitoring systems within 10 kilometers of a transiting vessel(s), that vessel must operate at 10 knots or less for 24 hours following the reported detection.
scope: 10 kilometers around transiting vessels, operational phase

requirement: LOA Holder's vessels, regardless of size, must immediately reduce speed to 10 kn or less when any large whale (other than a North Atlantic right whale) is observed within 500 meters of an underway vessel.
scope: 500 meters around underway vessels, operational phase

requirement: If LOA Holder's vessel(s) are traveling at speeds greater than 10 kn in a transit corridor from a port to the Lease Area, in addition to the required dedicated visual observer, LOA Holder must monitor the transit corridor in real-time with PAM prior to and during transits.
scope: Transit corridor from port to Lease Area, operational phase

requirement: If a North Atlantic right whale is detected via visual observation or PAM within or approaching the transit corridor, all crew transfer vessels must travel at 10 kn or less for 24 hours following the detection.
LOA Holder's vessels must maintain a minimum separation distance of 500 m from North Atlantic right whales.
If a North Atlantic right whale is sighted within 500 m of an underway vessel, that vessel must reduce speed and shift the engine to neutral.
LOA Holder's vessels must maintain a minimum separation distance of 100 m from sperm whales and non-North Atlantic right whale baleen whales.
LOA Holder's vessels must maintain a minimum separation distance of 50 m from all delphinoid cetaceans and pinnipeds.
When a marine mammal(s) is sighted while LOA Holder's vessel(s) is transiting, the vessel must take action as necessary to avoid violating the relevant separation distances.
LOA Holder's vessels underway must not divert or alter course to approach any marine mammal.
scope: Vessels operating in marine environments during construction activities.

requirement: If a plan is not submitted or approved by NMFS prior to vessel operations, all project vessels transiting, year round, must travel at speeds of 10-kn or less.
scope: Vessels operating in marine environments during construction activities.

requirement: Impact pile driving must not occur January 1 through April 30.
scope: Monopile and pin pile installation phase

requirement: Monopiles must be no larger than 11 m in diameter.
Hammer energies must not exceed 4,000 kilojoules for monopile installation.
No more than two monopiles may be installed per day.
Pin piles must be no larger than 5 m in diameter.
Hammer energies must not exceed 2,500 kJ for pin pile installation.
Impact pile driving must only be initiated during daylight hours in May and November.
scope: Impact pile driving in May and November

requirement: LOA Holder must utilize a soft-start protocol for each impact pile driving event.
Soft-start must occur at the beginning of impact driving and at any time following a cessation of impact pile driving of 30 minutes or longer.
Impact pile driving must be delayed until the animal has been visually observed exiting the clearance zone or until a specific time period has elapsed with no further sightings.
The clearance zone may only be declared clear if no North Atlantic right whale acoustic or visual detections have occurred within the clearance zone during the 60-minute monitoring period.
LOA Holder must deploy at least two functional noise abatement systems that reduce noise levels to the modeled harassment isopleths, assuming 10-dB attenuation, during all impact pile driving.
Any bubble curtain(s) must distribute air bubbles using an air flow rate of at least 0.5 m[3]/(minute*m).
The lowest bubble ring must be in contact with the seafloor for the full circumference of the ring, and the weights attached to the bottom ring must ensure 100-percent seafloor contact.
scope: Bubble curtain installation during construction phase.

requirement: No parts of the ring or other objects may prevent full seafloor contact with a bubble curtain ring.
scope: Bubble curtain installation during construction phase.

requirement: Construction contractors must train personnel in the proper balancing of airflow to the bubble curtain ring.
scope: Bubble curtain installation during construction phase.

requirement: LOA Holder must provide NMFS Office of Protected Resources with a bubble curtain performance test and maintenance report to review within 72 hours after each pile using a bubble curtain is installed.
scope: Bubble curtain installation during construction phase.

requirement: Corrections to the bubble ring(s) to meet the performance standards must occur prior to impact pile driving of monopiles.
scope: Bubble curtain installation prior to pile driving.

requirement: LOA Holder must utilize NMFS-approved PAM systems.
scope: PAM system deployment during construction phase.

requirement: The PAM system components must not be placed closer than 1 km to the pile being driven.
scope: PAM system deployment during construction phase.

requirement: The PAM system must be able to detect a vocalization of North Atlantic right whales up to 10 km.

If a marine mammal is detected (visually or acoustically) entering or within the respective shutdown zone after pile driving has begun, the PSO or PAM operator must call for a shutdown of pile driving and LOA Holder must stop pile driving immediately.
scope: Pile driving operations during construction phase.

requirement: If pile driving is not shutdown in one of these situations, LOA Holder must reduce hammer energy to the lowest level practicable and the reason(s) for not shutting down must be documented and reported to NMFS Office of Protected Resources.
scope: Pile driving operations during construction phase.

requirement: LOA Holder may request NMFS approval to use alternative technology (e.g., drones) in lieu of one or two of the dedicated PSO vessels that provide similar marine mammal detection capabilities.
scope: Marine mammal detection during construction phase.

requirement: If pile driving has been shut down due to the presence of a North Atlantic right whale, pile driving may not restart until the North Atlantic right whale has neither been visually or acoustically detected for 30 minutes.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: If pile driving has been shut down due to the presence of a marine mammal other than a North Atlantic right whale, pile driving must not restart until either the marine mammal(s) has voluntarily left the specific clearance zones and has been visually or acoustically confirmed beyond that clearance zone, or, when specific time periods have elapsed with no further sightings or acoustic detections have occurred.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: In cases where these criteria are not met, pile driving may restart only if necessary to maintain pile stability at which time LOA Holder must use the lowest hammer energy practicable to maintain stability.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: LOA Holder must conduct sound field verification (SFV) measurements during pile driving activities associated with the installation of, at minimum, the first three monopile foundations.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: SFV measurements must continue until at least three consecutive piles demonstrate noise levels are at or below those modeled, assuming 10 decibels (dB) of attenuation.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: Subsequent SFV measurements are also required should larger piles be installed or if additional piles are driven that may produce louder sound fields than those previously measured.
scope: Pile driving activities related to offshore wind farm construction.

requirement: The SFV measurement systems must have a sensitivity appropriate for the expected sound levels from pile driving received at the nominal ranges throughout the installation of the pile.
The frequency range of SFV measurement systems must cover the range of at least 20 hertz (Hz) to 20 kilohertz (kHz).

The dynamic range of the SFV measurement system must be sufficient such that at each location, and the signals avoid poor signal-to-noise ratios for low amplitude signals and avoid clipping, nonlinearity, and saturation for high amplitude signals.
All hydrophones used in SFV measurements systems are required to have undergone a full calibration.
LOA Holder must not exceed modeled distances to NMFS marine mammal Level A harassment and Level B harassment thresholds, assuming 10-dB attenuation, for foundation installation.

If any of the interim SFV measurement reports submitted for the first three monopiles indicate the modeled distances to NMFS marine mammal Level A harassment and Level B harassment thresholds assuming 10-dB attenuation, then LOA Holder must implement additional sound attenuation measures on all subsequent foundations.
LOA Holder must submit 48-hour interim reports after each foundation is measured.
LOA Holder must optimize the sound attenuation systems to meet noise levels modeled, assuming 10-dB attenuation, within three piles or else foundation installation activities must cease.

If acoustic measurements indicate that ranges to isopleths corresponding to the Level A harassment and Level B harassment thresholds are less than the ranges predicted by modeling, LOA Holder may request to NMFS Office of Protected Resources a modification of the clearance and shutdown zones.
LOA Holder must conduct SFV measurements upon commencement of turbine operations to estimate turbine operational source levels.

LOA Holder must submit a SFV Plan to NMFS Office of Protected Resources for review and approval at least 180 days prior to planned start of foundation installation activities and abide by the Plan if approved.
related_domains: marine mammal monitoring; sound attenuation; environmental impact assessment

requirement: The SFV Plan must describe how LOA Holder would ensure that the first three monopile foundation installation sites selected for SFV measurements are representative of the rest of the monopile installation sites.

In the case that these sites/scenarios are not determined to be representative of all other pile installation sites, LOA Holder must include information in the SFV Plan on how additional sites/scenarios would be selected for SFV measurements.
scope: Selection of additional sites for SFV measurements

requirement: The SFV Plan must also include methodology for collecting, analyzing, and preparing SFV measurement data for submission to NMFS Office of Protected Resources.
SFV for pile driving may not occur until NMFS approves the SFV Plan for this activity.

LOA Holder must submit a Passive Acoustic Monitoring Plan (PAM Plan) to NMFS Office of Protected Resources for review and approval at least 180 days prior to the planned start of foundation installation activities (impact pile driving) and abide by the Plan if approved.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection

requirement: No pile installation can occur if LOA Holder's PAM Plan does not receive approval from NMFS Office of Protected Resources and NMFS Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office Protected Resources Division.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection

requirement: Installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts must not occur during nighttime hours (defined as the hours between 1.5 hours prior to civil sunset and 1 hour after civil sunrise).
scope: Cofferdams and goal posts installation and removal

requirement: LOA Holder must stop vibratory pile driving immediately unless shutdown is not practicable due to imminent risk of injury or loss of life to an individual or if there is a risk of damage to the vessel that would create a risk of injury or loss of life for individuals or if the lead engineer determines there is refusal or instability.
scope: Vibratory pile driving associated with cofferdam and casing pipe installation

requirement: At least two on-duty PSOs must monitor for marine mammals at least 30 minutes before, during, and 30 minutes after vibratory pile driving associated with cofferdam and casing pipe installation.
scope: Vibratory pile driving associated with cofferdam and casing pipe installation

requirement: All installation and removal of sheet piles for cofferdams and casing pipes for goal posts must only occur for up to 12 hours for each cofferdam and up to 1 hour daily for each goal post.
scope: Installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts

requirement: LOA Holder must establish and implement clearance zones for the installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts using visual monitoring.
scope: Installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts

requirement: LOA Holder may only resort to high-order removal (i.e., detonation) if all other means of removal are impracticable.

LOA Holder may detonate a maximum of 10 UXO/MECs, of varying sizes but no larger than 1,000 pounds (lbs; 454 kilograms (kg)) charge weight (i.e., E12), over the effective period of this rulemaking and LOA.
LOA Holder must not detonate UXO/MECs from November 1 through April 31, annually.
UXO/MEC detonations must only occur during daylight hours.
No more than one detonation may occur within a 24-hour period.
LOA Holder must establish and implement clearance zones for UXO/MEC detonation using both visual and acoustic monitoring.
If the clearance zone is larger than 5 km, at least one dedicated PSO vessel (with at least three on-duty PSOs) and an aerial platform (with at least two on-duty PSOs) must be used.
LOA Holder must utilize NMFS-approved PAM systems.
LOA Holder must deploy at least a double big bubble curtain during all UXO/MEC detonations.
Construction contractors must train personnel in the proper balancing of airflow to the bubble curtain ring.
LOA Holder must provide NMFS Office of Protected Resources with a bubble curtain performance test and maintenance report to review within 72 hours after each UO/MEC is detonated.
Corrections to the bubble ring(s) to meet the performance standards in this paragraph (e)(9) must occur prior to UXO/MEC detonation.
LOA Holder must conduct SFV during all UXO/MEC detonations as described in paragraph (c)(15) of this section and deploy a pressure transducer.
Clearance zones must be fully visible for at least 60 minutes and all marine mammal(s) must be.

Detonation may only commence if all marine mammals have been confirmed to have voluntarily left the clearance zones and been visually confirmed to be beyond the clearance zone, or when 60 minutes have elapsed without any redetections for whales (including the North Atlantic right whale) or 15 minutes have elapsed without any redetections of delphinids, harbor porpoises, or seals.
LOA Holder must not exceed modeled distances to NMFS marine mammal Level A harassment and Level B harassment thresholds, assuming 10-dB attenuation, for UXO/MEC detonations.

If any of the interim SFV measurement reports submitted for any UXO/MEC detonations indicate the modeled distances to NMFS marine mammal Level A harassment and Level B harassment thresholds assuming 10-dB attenuation for future detonations will be exceeded, then LOA Holder must implement additional sound attenuation measures on all subsequent UXO/MEC detonations.

LOA Holder must also increase clearance zone sizes to those identified by NMFS until SFV measurements on UXO/MECs demonstrate distances to harassment thresholds will be met or will be less than those modeled.

LOA Holder must submit a SFV Plan for UXO/MEC detonation to NMFS Office of Protected Resources for review and approval at least 180 days prior to planned start of UXO/MEC detonation activities and abide by the Plan if approved.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; explosive ordnance disposal; environmental monitoring

requirement: SFV for UXO/MEC detonation cannot occur until NMFS approves the SFV Plan for this activity.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; explosive ordnance disposal

requirement: LOA Holder must submit a UXO/MEC Marine Mammal Monitoring Plan to NMFS Office of Protected Resources.

LOA Holder must obtain both NMFS Office of Protected Resources and NMFS Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office Protected Resources Division's concurrence with this Plan prior to the start of any UXO/MEC detonations.
The Plan must include a description of all monitoring equipment and PAM and PSO protocols (including number and location of PSOs) for all UXO/MEC detonations.

The PAM Plan must include a description of all proposed PAM equipment, address how the proposed passive acoustic monitoring must follow standardized measurement, processing methods, reporting metrics, and metadata standards for offshore wind.
No UXO/MEC detonations can occur without NMFS' approval of the Plan.
LOA Holder must establish and implement clearance and shutdown zones for HRG surveys using visual monitoring.
LOA Holder must utilize PSO(s), as described in § 217.265(f).
LOA Holder must abide by the relevant Project Design Criteria (PDCs 4, 5, and 7) of the programmatic consultation completed by NMFS' Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine life protection

requirement: SBPs must be deactivated when not acquiring data or preparing to acquire data, except as necessary for testing.
LOA Holder is required to ramp-up acoustic sources prior to commencing full power and ensure visual clearance zones are fully visible.
Prior to a ramp-up procedure starting or activating acoustic sources, the acoustic source operator must notify a designated PSO of the planned start of ramp-up as agreed upon with the Lead PSO.
During this 30-minute pre-start clearance period, the entire applicable clearance zones must be visible.
A PSO conducting pre-start clearance observations must be notified again immediately prior to reinitiating ramp-up procedures.
The LOA Holder must implement a 30-minute clearance period of the clearance zones immediately prior to the commencing of the survey.

If a marine mammal is observed within a clearance zone during the clearance period, ramp-up or acoustic surveys may not begin until the animal(s) has been observed voluntarily exiting its respective clearance zone or until a specific time period has elapsed with no further sighting.
The specific time period is 15 minutes for small odontocetes and pinnipeds, and 30 minutes for all other species.
Shutdown is required if a delphinid that belongs to a genus other than those specified in this paragraph is detected in the shutdown zone.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; environmental impact assessment

requirement: If an acoustic source has been shut down due to the presence of a marine mammal, the use of an acoustic source may not commence or resume until the animal(s) has been confirmed to have left the Level B harassment zone or until a full 15 minutes (for small odontocetes and seals) or 30 minutes (for all other marine mammals) have elapsed with no further sighting.
scope: Level B harassment zone during survey operations

requirement: LOA Holder must immediately shut down any acoustic source if a marine mammal is sighted entering or within its respective shutdown zones.
scope: Shutdown zones related to acoustic sources during construction activities.

requirement: Shutdown is required if a delphinid that belongs to a genus other than those specified in paragraph (f)(12) of this section is detected in the shutdown zone.
scope: Shutdown zones related to delphinid detection during construction activities.

requirement: If an acoustic source is shut down for a period longer than 30 minutes, all clearance and ramp-up procedures must be initiated.
scope: Operational procedures following acoustic source shutdown.

requirement: Gear must not be deployed if there is a risk of interaction with marine mammals.
scope: Fishery monitoring surveys during construction activities.

requirement: Gear may be deployed after 15 minutes of no marine mammal sightings within 1 nautical mile of the sampling station.
scope: Fishery monitoring surveys during construction activities.

requirement: If marine mammals are sighted within 1 nmi of the planned location and 15 minutes before gear deployment, then LOA Holder and/or its cooperating institutions, contracted vessels, or commercially hired captains must move the vessel away from the marine mammal to a different section of the sampling area.
If a marine mammal is deemed to be at risk of interaction after the gear is deployed or set, all gear must be immediately removed from the water.
All fisheries monitoring gear must be fully cleaned and repaired (if damaged) before each use/deployment.
LOA Holder's fixed gear must comply with the Atlantic Large Whale Take Reduction Plan regulations.
Trawl tows must be limited to a maximum of a 20-minute trawl time at 3.0 kn.
During trawl surveys, vessel crew must open the codend of the trawl net close to the deck in order to avoid injury to animals that may be caught in the gear.
Baited remote underwater video (BRUV) sampling must limit soak duration to 60 minutes or less.
scope: In-water survey gear usage during construction.

requirement: Each chevron trap must have a vertical buoy line and must limit soak duration to 90 minutes or less.
scope: In-water survey gear usage during construction.

requirement: All fishery survey-related lines must include the breaking strength of all lines being less than 1,700 pounds (lbs).
scope: In-water survey gear usage during construction.

requirement: Buoy lines must utilize weak links. Weak links must break cleanly leaving behind the bitter end of the line.
scope: In-water survey gear usage during construction.

requirement: All in-water survey gear, including buoys, must be properly labeled with the scientific permit number or identification as LOA Holder's research gear.
scope: In-water survey gear usage during construction.

requirement: LOA Holder must use independent, NMFS-approved PSOs and PAM operators.
All PSOs and PAM operators must have successfully attained a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with a major in one of the natural sciences.
Requests for such a waiver must be submitted to NMFS Office of Protected Resources and must include written justification containing alternative experience.
PSOs must have visual acuity in both eyes (with correction of vision being permissible) sufficient.
All PSOs must be trained in northwestern Atlantic Ocean marine mammal identification and behaviors and must be able to conduct field observations and collect data according to assigned protocols.
PSOs and PAM operators must successfully complete a relevant training course within the last 5 years, including obtaining a certificate of course completion.
scope: General, applicable to PSOs and PAM operators

requirement: Lead PSO or PAM operators must be unconditionally approved and have a minimum of 90 days in a northwestern Atlantic Ocean offshore environment performing the role.
scope: Northwestern Atlantic Ocean offshore environment, PSO and PAM operator roles.

requirement: LOA Holder must submit NMFS previously approved PSOs and PAM operators to NMFS Office of Protected Resources for review and confirmation of their approval for specific roles at least 30 days prior to commencement of the activities requiring PSOs/PAM operators.

LOA Holder must submit NMFS previously approved PSOs and PAM operators to NMFS Office of Protected Resources for review and confirmation of their approval for specific roles 15 days prior to when new PSOs/PAM operators are required after activities have commenced.
PAM operators are responsible for obtaining NMFS approval.

PAM operators must demonstrate that they have prior experience with real-time acoustic detection systems and/or have completed specialized training for operating PAM systems and detecting and identifying Atlantic Ocean marine mammals sounds.

PAM operators must be able to distinguish between whether a marine mammal or other species sound is detected, possibly detected, not detected and similar terminology must be used across companies/projects.
PAM operators need to have demonstrated experience in using localization techniques for sounds.
PAM operators must have the qualifications and relevant experience/training to safely deploy and retrieve equipment and program the software, as necessary.
PAM operators must be able to test software and hardware functionality prior to operation.

PAM operators must have evaluated their acoustic detection software using the PAM Atlantic baleen whale annotated data set available at National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) and provide evaluation/performance metric.

PAM operators must be able to review and classify acoustic detections in real-time (prioritizing North Atlantic right whales and noting detection of other cetaceans) during the real-time monitoring periods.

PSOs may work as PAM operators and vice versa, pending NMFS-approval; however, they may only perform one role at any one time and must not exceed work time restrictions, which must be tallied cumulatively.
PSOs must monitor for marine mammals prior to, during, and following impact pile driving, vibratory pile driving, UXO/MEC detonation activities, and HRG surveys.
scope: Construction phase, specifically during impact pile driving, vibratory pile driving, UXO/MEC detonation activities, and HRG surveys.

requirement: For foundation installation and UXO/MEC detonation, PSOs must visually clear the entire minimum visibility zone for a full 30 minutes immediately prior to commencing activities.
scope: Foundation installation and UXO/MEC detonation activities.

requirement: All PSOs must be located at the best vantage point(s) on any platform to obtain 360-degree visual coverage of the entire clearance and shutdown zones.
scope: Construction phase, specifically during activities requiring PSO monitoring.

requirement: The PAM operator must monitor to and past the clearance zone for large whales.
scope: Clearance and shutdown zones during construction activities.

requirement: All on-duty PSOs must remain in real-time contact with the on-duty PAM operator(s).
PAM operators must immediately communicate all acoustic detections of marine mammals to PSOs.
The PAM operator must inform the Lead PSO(s) on duty of animal detections approaching or within applicable ranges of interest.
PSOs must use high magnification (25x) binoculars, standard handheld (7x) binoculars.

PSOs and PAM operators must not exceed 4 consecutive watch hours on duty at any time, must have a 2-hour (minimum) break between watches, and must not exceed a combined watch schedule of more than 12 hours in a 24-hour period.
scope: Monitoring during WTG and OSS foundation installation and UXO/MEC detonations

requirement: PSOs on the pile driving and detonation-dedicated PSO vessel must be equipped with functional Big Eye binoculars.
PAM operators must have a computer station equipped with a data collection software system available wherever they are stationed.
scope: Monitoring during WTG and OSS foundation installation and UXO/MEC detonations

requirement: During periods of low visibility, PSOs must use alternative technology (i.e., infrared or thermal cameras) to monitor the clearance and shutdown zones as approved by NMFS.
scope: Monitoring during WTG and OSS foundation installation and UXO/MEC detonations

requirement: At least three on-duty PSOs must be stationed and observing from the activity platform during impact pile driving or UXO/MEC detonation.
scope: Impact pile driving and UXO/MEC detonation activities.

requirement: The PAM operator must review all detections from the previous 24-hour period immediately prior to pile driving and UXO/MEC detonation activities.
scope: Prior to pile driving or UXO/MEC detonation activities.

requirement: At least two PSOs must be on active duty during all activities related to the installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts.
scope: Installation and removal of cofferdams and goal posts.

requirement: PSOs must monitor the clearance zone for the presence of marine mammals for 30 minutes before, throughout the installation of the sheet piles (and casing pipe, if installed), and for 30 minutes after all vibratory pile driving activities have ceased.
scope: Installation of sheet piles and casing pipe during construction phase.

requirement: Sheet pile or casing pipe installation must only commence when visual clearance zones are fully visible and clear of marine mammals, as determined by the Lead PSO, for at least 30 minutes immediately prior to initiation of vibratory pile driving.
scope: Installation of sheet piles and casing pipe during construction phase.

requirement: Between four and six PSOs must be present on every 24-hour survey vessel and two to three PSOs must be present on every 12-hour survey vessel.
At least one PSO must be on active duty monitoring during HRG surveys conducted during daylight and at least two PSOs must be on active duty monitoring during HRG surveys conducted at night.
scope: HRG surveys conducted during daylight and night.

requirement: PSOs on HRG vessels must begin monitoring 30 minutes prior to activating acoustic sources, during the use of these acoustic sources, and for 30 minutes after use of these acoustic sources has ceased.
related_domains: marine mammal monitoring; acoustic source management

requirement: Any observations of marine mammals must be communicated to PSOs on all nearby survey vessels during concurrent HRG surveys.

During daylight hours when survey equipment is not operating, LOA Holder must ensure that visual PSOs conduct observations for comparison of sighting rates and behavior with and without use of the specified acoustic sources.

Marine mammal monitoring must be conducted within 1 nmi from the planned survey location by the trained captain and/or a member of the scientific crew for 15 minutes prior to deploying gear, throughout gear deployment and use, and for 15 minutes after haul back.
scope: 1 nautical mile from the planned survey location during fishery surveys.

requirement: LOA Holder must use a standardized reporting system during the effective period of the LOA.
scope: Reporting of data collected related to the Project.

requirement: All data collected related to the Project must be recorded using industry-standard software that is installed on field laptops and/or tablets.
scope: Data collection and reporting for the Project.

requirement: All reports must be submitted to NMFS Office of Protected Resources, dates must be in MM/DD/YYYY format, and location information must be provided in Decimal Degrees and with the coordinate system information.
scope: Submission of reports related to the Project.

requirement: All marine mammal sightings, regardless of distance from the construction activity, must be reported.
The description of any mitigation-related action implemented, or mitigation-related actions called for but not implemented, in response to the sighting must be reported.

LOA Holder must compile and submit weekly reports during foundation installation to NMFS Office of Protected Resources that document the daily start and stop of all pile driving associated with the Project; the start and stop of associated observation periods by PSOs; details on the deployment of PSOs; a record of all detections of marine mammals (acoustic and visual); any mitigation actions (or if mitigation actions could not be taken, provide reasons why); and details on the noise attenuation system(s) used and its performance.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; construction monitoring; noise management

requirement: Weekly reports are due on Wednesday for the previous week (Sunday to Saturday) and must include the information required under this section.
The weekly report must also identify which turbines become operational and when (a map must be provided).
Monthly reports are due on the 15th of the month for the previous month.
scope: Project activities and marine mammal detections during construction phase.
source: NMFS North Atlantic Right Whale Passive Acoustic Reporting System

requirement: Full PAM detection data and metadata must also be submitted monthly on the 15th of every month for the previous month.

must provide the initial results of the SFV measurements to NMFS Office of Protected Resources in an interim report after each foundation installation event and each UXO/MEC detonation event as soon as they are available and prior to a subsequent detonation or foundation installation, but no later than 48 hours after each completed foundation installation event and 48 hours after a detonation.

related_domains: marine mammal protection; construction reporting; acoustic monitoring

requirement: The report must include, at minimum: hammer energies/schedule used during pile driving, including, the total number of strikes and the maximum hammer energy.

The report must include, at minimum: peak sound pressure level (SPL pk), root-mean-square sound pressure level that contains 90 percent of the acoustic energy (SPL rms), and sound exposure level (SEL, in single strike for pile driving, SEL ss), for each hydrophone, including at least the maximum, arithmetic mean, minimum.

If any in-situ calibration checks for hydrophones reveal a calibration drift greater than 0.75 dB, LOA Holder must indicate full details of the calibration procedure, results, and any associated issues in the 48-hour interim reports.
scope: Hydrophone calibration during construction and operation phases.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; marine mammal protection; regulatory compliance

requirement: The final reports must include all details prescribed above for the interim report as well as, at minimum, the following: the peak sound pressure level (SPL pk), the root-mean-square sound pressure level that contains 90 percent of the acoustic energy (SPL rms), the single strike sound exposure level (SEL ss), the integration time for SPL rms, the spectrum, and the 24-hour cumulative SEL extrapolated from measurements at all hydrophones.
scope: Final reporting phase for offshore wind farm activities.

requirement: The final report must also include at least the maximum, mean, minimum, median (L 50) and L 5 (95 percent exceedance) statistics for each metric.
scope: Final reporting phase for offshore wind farm activities.

requirement: The sound levels reported must be in median, arithmetic mean, and L 5 (95 percent exceedance) (i.e., average in linear space), and in dB.
scope: Final reporting phase for offshore wind farm activities.

requirement: The extents of the measured Level A harassment and Level B harassment zone(s) must be reported.
scope: Final reporting phase for offshore wind farm activities.

requirement: A description of the noise abatement system and operational parameters (e.g., bubble flow rate, distance deployed from the pile and/or UXO/MEC, etc.) must be included.

LOA Holder must report any lost gear associated with the fishery surveys to the NMFS GARFO Protected Resources Division as soon as possible or within 24 hours of the documented time of missing or lost gear.
To incidentally take marine mammals pursuant to this subpart, LOA Holder must apply for and obtain an LOA.
The LOA must set forth... means of effecting the least practicable adverse impact (i.e., mitigation) on the species, its habitat, and on the availability of the species for subsistence uses.
scope: All phases of activity under the LOA.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; species protection; habitat conservation

requirement: In the event of projected changes to the activity or to mitigation and monitoring measures required by an LOA, LOA Holder must apply for and obtain a modification of the LOA.
Issuance of the LOA must be based on a determination that the level of taking must be consistent with the findings made for the total taking allowable under the regulations of this subpart.
Notice of issuance or denial of an LOA must be published in the FEDERAL REGISTER within 30 days of a determination.

The LOA shall be modified, provided that NMFS Office of Protected Resources determines that the changes to the activity or the mitigation, monitoring, or reporting do not change the findings made for the regulations in this subpart and do not result in more than a minor change in the total estimated number of takes.
Through adaptive management, NMFS Office of Protected Resources may modify (including delete, modify, or add to) the existing mitigation, monitoring, or reporting measures.
scope: Mitigation and monitoring measures under LOA

requirement: If, through adaptive management, the modifications to the mitigation, monitoring, or reporting measures are substantial, NMFS Office of Protected Resources shall publish a notice of proposed LOA in the FEDERAL REGISTER and solicit public comment.
scope: Mitigation, monitoring, or reporting measures related to marine mammals.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; environmental impact assessment

requirement: If NMFS Office of Protected Resources determines that an emergency exists that poses a significant risk to the well-being of the species or stocks of marine mammals specified in the LOA issued, an LOA may be modified without prior notice or opportunity for public comment.
scope: Emergency modifications to LOA concerning marine mammals.
